title: Perfect Game Middle East Expansion Names VICE Baseball Country Partner Across Four Gulf Nations
article_text:
- Perfect Game named VICE Baseball its Country Partner for the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Kuwait, with the first event set for Dubai in December 2026.

- A major international tournament follows in March 2027 and will bring together teams from around the world, according to Perfect Game.

- The Gulf deal was announced one week after Perfect Game revealed a new country partnership in China, its second international move in consecutive weeks.

- Kash Shaikh, Perfect Game’s Chief Marketing Officer and Head of International, previously co-founded Dubai-based Baseball United and spent four years in Dubai.

The business of youth sports, first in your search results.

Perfect Game, which describes itself as the world’s largest youth baseball and softball platform and scouting service, announced on November 24, 2026 its expansion into the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region. The company named VICE Baseball as its Country Partner for the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Kuwait. Starting in December 2026, VICE will run Perfect Game tournaments, clinics and showcases across all four countries, beginning with an event in Dubai.

The Dubai event opens the schedule, and Perfect Game said a major international tournament will follow in March 2027, bringing together teams from around the world.

Between those dates, VICE plans to work with local baseball organizations, academies and teams to build a regular event calendar and encourage participation across age groups, according to the announcement. Showcases will give players a way to demonstrate their skills and gain visibility through Perfect Game’s international platform.

The company said the long-term goal is a sustainable regional circuit that connects baseball communities, raises the level of competition and gives young athletes a clearer path to advance in the sport.

The GCC announcement came one week after Perfect Game named JinMu Sports as its exclusive Country Partner in China.

VICE Baseball is a subsidiary of VICE Sports Group, led by Tony Khoury. The company is a U.S.-based youth baseball development organization with roots in Katy, Texas. Under the partnership, VICE will pair its player development work with Perfect Game’s tournament and scouting platform.

VICE’s baseball operations are led by David McDaniel, who has more than 20 years of coaching experience, per the release. McDaniel played professionally as a catcher in the Cleveland Indians, Detroit Tigers and Texas Rangers organizations. He later coached with the Sugar Land Skeeters, now the Sugar Land Space Cowboys, and helped guide Texas high school teams to state championships.

What Does the Partnership Give Gulf Players?

The core offer is scouting access. Khoury said college coaches and professional scouts will have direct access to player profiles and stats through Perfect Game, and that VICE expects some of them to attend future events in the region.

“That gives our players the same kind of scouting exposure as players in the U.S.,” Khoury said. “We’re grateful for Perfect Game’s trust in VICE and the chance to build something lasting for players and families across the region.”

The expansion is led on Perfect Game’s side by Kash Shaikh, the company’s Chief Marketing Officer and Head of International. Shaikh is the former chairman, CEO and co-founder of Dubai-based Baseball United.

“After spending the last four years in Dubai working to build the baseball ecosystem with my previous league, I realized that we needed to do more to help a greater number of young athletes fall in love with the game,” Shaikh said. He added that Perfect Game plans to partner with groups already active in the region’s baseball community.

The first test of that plan is the Dubai event in December. The bigger one comes in March 2027, when the international tournament will show how many college coaches and scouts make the trip to the region.

American families spend approximately $54 billion annually on kids’ sports and recreation, according to the YSBR and Kinetica Group Youth Sports TAM & Parent Spending Report, with organized sports alone representing a $40 billion-plus market. The average family spent $1,016 on a child’s primary sport in 2024, up 46 percent since 2019, per the Aspen Institute’s Project Play, and market research projects the global youth sports market will reach approximately $114 billion by 2032 (Business Research Insights).

How many kids play youth sports in the United States?

Approximately 27.3 million children ages 6 to 17, or about 54.6 percent, played organized sports in 2022-2023, according to the National Survey of Children’s Health as reported by the Aspen Institute’s Project Play. High school sports participation reached a record 8.26 million athletes in 2024-25, per the NFHS.

title: Usha International extends partnership with MI Emirates for the 2026–27 season
article_text:
New Delhi: Usha International, one of India’s most trusted consumer durables brands, has now extended its 13-year partnership with the MI Global Family to also take forward its association with MI Emirates for the 5th year running. As the official sponsor for the 2026–27 season of the UAE International T20 League, the brand reinforces its commitment to promoting sporting excellence and active lifestyles through the power of sport. The continued association further strengthens Usha’s presence on the international cricket stage.

The month-long league will feature six teams competing in 34 matches across Abu Dhabi, Dubai and Sharjah. The tournament will bring together leading cricketing talent for an action-packed season, with matches broadcast globally by Zee Entertainment across its linear television channels and OTT platform, ZEE5, connecting the tournament with a wider audience of cricket fans.

Speaking about the continued association, Komal Mehra, Head – Sports Initiatives & Associations, Usha International, said, “Our continued association with MI Emirates reflects Usha’s enduring commitment to furthering the power that sports wield in bringing together communities of people with passion for the game, transcending age, gender, and borders. Cricket enjoys an extraordinary following across geographies, and this partnership provides us with a great platform to strengthen our engagement with fans in the UAE and beyond. While celebrating the game and our partnership we also look forward to creating meaningful fan experiences that create cherished memories for them.”

The MI Emirates spokesperson added, “It’s heartening to have Usha International continue its association with us across countries, and we are delighted to welcome them as the Official Partner for the season. Our shared passion for cricket and commitment to creating engaging experiences for fans make this a strong partnership. Over the past four seasons, we have consistently focused on engaging with our fans and the wider community, and we look forward to continuing these efforts and strengthening those connections throughout the season.”

With MI Emirates gearing up for an exciting season, Usha is deepening its engagement across multiple touchpoints. As part of the association, Usha will organise exclusive meet-and-greet sessions with select MI Emirates players, alongside digital activations on the team’s social media platforms, including the ‘Pick the Wrong’Un’ and ‘Player of the Match’ contests, as well as signed memorabilia giveaways for fans. The association will also include match-day entitlements including hospitality and general tickets

Usha has been a strong advocate for inclusive sports initiatives across India. Beyond its affiliation with MI Emirates, the brand actively supports Ultimate Flying Disc, Football, Ladies Amateur and Junior Golf, Cricket for the Deaf, and various sports for the visually challenged, including athletics, kabaddi, judo, and powerlifting. Usha is also deeply committed to reviving indigenous Indian sports such as Kalaripayattu, Mallakhamb, Siat Khnam, Thang-Ta, Turai Kabaddi, Saz-Loung, Mardani Khel, Yoga, Yubi Lakpi, Aki Kiti, Atya Patya, Paika Akhada, Chhinj, and Silambam.

For more information, please visit www.usha.com and www.ushaplay.com. Catch action updates on UshaPlay, follow @UshaPlay on Twitter and @usha_play on Instagram.

title: Senegal vs Morocco Afcon verdict: CAS ruling explained and what happens next
article_text:
Senegal were reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners on Tuesday after sport's highest court upheld their appeal against being stripped of the title, ruling that the referee's decision to resume the match was covered by the “field of play” doctrine.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) panel set aside the Confederation of African Football (CAF) Appeal Board's decision that had forfeited Senegal's 1-0 extra-time win and awarded Morocco a 3-0 result.

The CAF said in a statement it “respects the CAS award and will take all the necessary measures to implement it”.

The panel found that “the referee [Jean-Jacques Ndala of the Democratic Republic of Congo] did not commit any error of law”, CAS Secretary General Matthieu Reeb said.

CAS confirmed the result of the January 18 final in Rabat as 1-0 to Senegal.

The Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) said the decision was a triumph for “sporting fairness” and that the “outcome of a match is determined solely on the field of play, under the protection of sports law”.

FSF President Abdoulaye Fall said the federation was ready to put the matter behind it and offered an olive branch to its Moroccan counterparts.

“The Court of ‌Arbitration for Sport has delivered justice for sport,” Fall said in a statement. “I wish to strongly reaffirm the bonds of brotherhood that unite us with the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) and the Moroccan people.

“Senegalese football now looks firmly towards the future with confidence and enthusiasm in an Africa united around the values of sport.”

Senegal walked off the pitch for 14 minutes in the final after a penalty awarded against them late in regulation time. The players returned before the match resumed, Morocco missed the spot kick and Pape Gueye scored the winner in extra time.

CAS said the referee's decision to resume play fell within his sole authority, and that the effects of that decision were limited to the pitch.

Morocco's federation had argued that the referee's decision fell outside the field of play doctrine and that the walk-off breached Articles 82 and 84 of the Cup of Nations regulations.

Those articles apply only when a referee calls off a match permanently, the panel said, so did not apply here.

The panel acknowledged the referee made his decision under extreme tension but said that did not justify calling it “arbitrary.”

The panel also said that CAF had already sanctioned the FSF, Senegal's then-coach Pape Thiaw and players Iliman Ndiaye and Ismaila Sarr in separate disciplinary proceedings.

The FRMF said in a statement that it will contest the decision, alleging there had been contact between its Senegalese counterpart and CAS arbitrator Ulrich Haas in the days leading up to the verdict.

However, an FSF spokesperson told Reuters: “That is false. There was no telephone contact on Sunday or on any other day.”

CAS added: “Ulrich Haas strongly denies any direct contact at any moment with the parties involved in this procedure”.

The FRMF said it will “initiate all necessary legal ‌proceedings to challenge the CAS decision” after it complained about alleged contact made between FSF President Fall and CAS arbitrator Haas 48 hours before the ruling was issued.

It can do so by appealing to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court, which is the only court with jurisdiction to hear the challenge.

French sports law expert Gerald ‌Simon chaired the CAS panel, with assistance from Italian international law professor Luigi Fumagalli and Haas, a Hamburg-based attorney and professor of law at the University of Zurich.

“There could only be one winner in this final, just as there could only be one winner in this legal process,” CAS's Reeb told reporters. “The law has spoken. I think we simply have to accept the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

“The team's [Senegal's] temporary withdrawal from the field was not followed by the abandonment of the match. If the referee had blown the final whistle, he could have done so, and perhaps things would have turned out differently. The CAS arbitrators considered that the referee was within his rights,” he added.

Senegal striker Sadio Mane said he hoped the matter did not drive a wedge between the two nations. The Al Nassr forward was instrumental in persuading his team to return to the pitch in the final.

“I send a message of respect and encouragement to the Moroccan people and the players of Morocco,” Mane said in a statement.

“They've done a great course and can be proud of it. I wish them all the best for the future. Senegal and Morocco are two brotherly peoples. May the passion of football continue to bring us closer.”

title: NFL reportedly wants Paramount to increase rights fee north of 50-60 percent
article_text:
The incumbent NFL broadcasters may end up paying at least 50 percent more — amounting to in excess of $3.0 billion a year each — simply to keep their rights through the end of the originally negotiated terms.

The NFL is seeking a rights fee increase north of 50-60 percent as part of its media rights negotiations with CBS parent company Paramount Skydance, with that range representing the “midpoint” between what the league is seeking and what it is currently being offered, according to Alex Sherman of CNBC. A 50 percent increase would raise the current CBS rights fee of $2.1 billion/year past the $3 billion mark.

As John Ourand of Puck reported last week, the new rights fees will kick in immediately upon the completion of any deal. The league is expected to negotiate its renewals one-by-one, starting with Paramount and then Fox, per Ourand.

The new report Friday was the first concrete indication of where the NFL might set the market for its expedited media rights negotiations. A 50 percent increase across the board would take each of the league’s broadcast network rights deals past the $3 billion mark, with Disney paying more than $4 billion. But Amazon, which is paying just $1.0 billion/year for its main “Thursday Night Football” package, would still be paying less than $2 billion.

There is no reason to believe the NFL would seek consistent increases across the board, as it has not done so in past negotiations. In the 2011 media rights talks, Disney agreed to pay nearly twice as much for NFL rights ($1.9B/year) as any of the other networks (FOX was second-highest a $1.1B/year). When those rights were renewed in 2021, CBS, NBC and FOX saw their rights fees double, while Disney — which remained the highest-paying rightsholder — came away with a comparably modest 40 percent increase. One can envision a repeat in the upcoming negotiations, as it is hard to imagine that Prime Video will continue paying half as much as the other networks.

Notably, any eventual deal cannot be accurately described as a media rights ‘extension.’ Per Sherman, the NFL is agreeing only to waive the opt-out provision it could otherwise exercise in 2029. And while it has long been assumed that the NFL would exercise that opt-out, the fact is that those 2021 media rights deals were always set to run through the 2033-34 season. In agreeing to negotiate early, the networks are merely guaranteeing that they will have rights for as long as was originally negotiated.

title: WSL makes agreement with clubs to avoid gambling sponsors
article_text:
WSL Football, the organisation responsible for operating the top two tiers of women's football in the UK, has reached an agreement in principle for its clubs not to make sponsorship deals with betting companies.

Instead, the organisation has agreed to pursue sponsorship deals with brands from different industries, reports The Athletic. The outlet states that six additional sponsorship opportunities were made available ahead of the 2024/25 season, and these were filled by Apple, Airbnb, British Gas, Mercedes, Tesco and WTW.

While the agreement applies to WSL Football's own commercial partnerships, it does not stop individual WSL or WSL2 clubs from signing sponsorship deals with gambling companies.

Rather, it sets a different direction for WSL Football's league-level partnerships, giving the leagues the chance to shape their own commercial future. The organisation wants to continue aiding the growth of the women's domestic game, while combating issues such as player welfare, gambling-related online abuse and fluctuating attendances.

The changes also come at a time when English football is starting to take a wider look at gambling and related sponsorships. At the start of this season, the Premier League's voluntary ban on betting sponsors appearing on the front of match-day shirts came into effect, while the Premier League, EFL, FA and WSL also introduced a Code of Conduct for gambling-related sponsorship agreements in 2024.

Nevertheless, betting companies still feature prominently among sponsors at clubs throughout the top divisions in the men's game, with Betway signing a deal with Manchester United and clubs such as Leeds and Nottingham Forest also agreeing new deals over the summer.

title: Rights to next WBC will be negotiated alongside broader MLB package
article_text:
Coming off of a record-setting performance in the United States, negotiations for rights to the next World Baseball Classic will coincide with Major League Baseball’s broader media rights talks.

Rights to broadcast the next World Baseball Classic will be negotiated alongside the broader Major League Baseball rights packages in 2028, Sports Media Watch has learned. WBC rights have historically been sold separately, but MLB will have the opportunity to add the WBC to conversations that are already expected to include its full suite of local, national and global rights.

MLB commissioner Rob Manfred signaled as much on “The Dan Patrick Show” earlier this month: “Our broadcast partners were out in force at the WBC finals and I think this is going to be a piece of our national broadcasting agreements.”

Manfred conditioned that statement on the event shifting to a regular rotation: “Obviously to do that it has to be on a regular schedule.” The WBC has taken place every three or four years since its inception in 2006, and it is not immediately clear whether the next edition will be in 2029 or 2030.

Rights to this past year’s WBC were officially set mere months in advance, with Fox Sports’ deal to acquire U.S. rights announced last October. It is unclear whether the company had any competition for the event, which ended up delivering audiences in the neighborhood of World Series games.

Netflix had previously secured Japanese rights to the event in a deal announced last August.

Both Fox and Netflix are incumbent MLB rights partners and will presumably be at the negotiating table in 2028. There are six total incumbents heading into 2028, with Fox and Netflix joined by NBCUniversal, TNT Sports, Apple and ESPN — the latter of which was the initial English-language broadcast partner for the WBC in 2006 and 2009.

MLB also has a partnership with TelevisaUnivision, which has carried Game 1 of the World Series in each of the past two seasons and this past year shared WBC rights in Mexico with Disney.

The league is also widely expected to at least attempt to bundle its full suite of local rights into a centralized package, presumably drawing streamers to the table who do not currently own rights.

title: Lakers ink sponsorship deal with Kalshi
article_text: The Lakers have named Kalshi the team’s official prediction market sponsor. Kalshi is an NBA preferred prediction market exchange (Lakers). The Hawks had signed PrizePicks as a sponsor, making it the first pick ‘em and prediction market operator to sponsor an NBA team, but its deal precluded it from promoting its prediction market offerings through the Hawks (SBJ).

title: Maincast Sport secures WTA broadcast rights in Ukraine
article_text:
Maincast Sport has acquired the rights to broadcast the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz in Ukraine under a long-term agreement, bringing the world's leading women's professional tennis tour to Ukrainian audiences with dedicated Ukrainian-language coverage.

The agreement will give fans access to Ukrainian-language coverage of WTA tournaments throughout the 2027 season, as the Tour visits 26 countries and territories. From Brisbane and Auckland in January, the season will take in iconic destinations including Indian Wells, Miami, Madrid, Rome and Beijing, culminating in the season-ending FAGE WTA Finals in Charlotte, USA, in November.

The WTA Tour joins Maincast Sport’s portfolio of international sports properties including the NBA, Copa del Rey, MotoGP and NASCAR. Now with the WTA, the addition further strengthens Maincast Sport’s offering, bringing fans world-class women’s tennis and the opportunity to follow the Ukrainian players who consistently compete at the highest level.

The partnership includes: International WTA 1000 events, WTA 500 Events, WTA 250 Events, and the FAGE WTA Finals taking place in Charlotte (USA), where the season’s top eight singles players and doubles teams will compete.

“Tennis is one of the sports where Ukraine has genuine stars, and fans have followed every match our players have played for years. From 2027, matches featuring Elina Svitolina, Marta Kostyuk, Dayana Yastremska and other Ukrainian players will be available exclusively on Maincast Sport, alongside hundreds of matches from the world’s best players. We’re creating our own tennis shows, analysis and broadcasts with star guests. The WTA calendar runs almost all year round, so Maincast Sport viewers will get top-level tennis every week,,” said Vitalii Volochai, co-founder of Maincast.

“We’re delighted to partner with Maincast Sport to bring more women’s tennis to fans in Ukraine, where the sport already means so much. Ukrainian players continue to make an important impact on the global stage, and this agreement will give fans more opportunities to follow their favourite athletes and experience the excitement of the WTA Tour throughout the season,” said Marina Storti, CEO of WTA Ventures.

WTA Tour matches will be available to fans on the Maincast Sport TV channel and Maincast.tv platform.

title: Alba Larsen targets 2027 F1 Academy title after Vegas
article_text:
Alba Larsen has set her sights on the 2027 F1 ACADEMY title after ending her season with a win and a second place in Las Vegas. The Ferrari-backed MP Motorsport driver beat champion Alisha Palmowski from ninth on the grid in the reverse-grid race, then traded the lead with her in the feature race before a late Safety Car ended their fight.

Larsen will return for a third season in the series, with Ferrari continuing its backing. The 17-year-old finished fourth in the 2026 standings on 104 points, scoring 80 of them across the final three rounds.

Larsen started ninth in Friday’s reverse-grid race after serving a three-place penalty carried over from Austin. She passed Palmowski on lap two and moved into the lead by lap five. Two Safety Car periods gave Palmowski chances to get back on terms, but Larsen held her off to win from the lowest starting position in series history.

From the front row on Saturday, Larsen used Palmowski’s slipstream to go around the outside at Turn 2 on lap two. Palmowski took the lead back later in the lap and stayed ahead when they went side by side again on the main straight on lap six.

Larsen lost ground with a lock-up at the restart. When Lisa Billard hit the wall on lap 12, the Safety Car came out again and stayed on track to the finish. Larsen crossed the line 0.320 seconds behind Palmowski and told F1 ACADEMY she had wanted one more chance to attack. She credited Palmowski’s defending throughout their duel.

Larsen took six podiums in the final seven races, including her first series win in Austin. She said that run gave her and the team confidence heading into winter preparation. Racing the champion for wins gave her a benchmark for the season ahead.

“Winning the title is the goal for next year,” Larsen told F1 ACADEMY.

Palmowski will move up to Formula Regional with Rodin Motorsport in 2027. For Larsen, the task is to carry her late-season form into the opening rounds, where she scored just 24 points across the first half of 2026.

title: Major League Fishing Announces Multi-Year Sponsorship Renewal with Tackle Warehouse
article_text:
BENTON, Ky. (Nov. 24, 2026) – Major League Fishing (MLF) announced today a multiyear sponsorship renewal with Tackle Warehouse, a leading online retailer of fishing tackle and equipment. The three-year agreement extends the companies’ longstanding partnership, with Tackle Warehouse continuing as the title sponsor of the Tackle Warehouse Pro Circuit and an Official Tackle Retailer of MLF5.

A valued MLF partner since 2020, Tackle Warehouse has played an integral role in supporting competitive bass fishing across multiple levels of the sport. The renewed agreement reinforces the retailer’s commitment to tournament anglers while maintaining its prominent presence throughout MLF’s professional and grassroots tournament platforms.

The 2027 Tackle Warehouse Pro Circuit will showcase top professional anglers competing across six premier fisheries for the sport’s biggest payouts outside of the Bass Pro Tour, valuable points toward Pro Circuit Championship qualification and opportunities to advance to REDCREST and the Bass Pro Tour.

“Tournament fishing has always been an important part of who we are at Tackle Warehouse, and our partnership with Major League Fishing allows us to stay closely connected to the action and help drive this sport forward,” said Joey Reggio, General Manager at Tackle Warehouse. “We’re proud to back a circuit that gives anglers a real shot at their dreams and gives fans a front-row seat to some of the best tournament bass fishing anywhere.  We’re anglers ourselves, and we’re excited to keep supporting the sport we love.”

Tackle Warehouse will maintain brand visibility across all MLF5 media platforms, including television airings on VICE TV and MLFNOW! livestream coverage on MajorLeagueFishing.com, the MyOutdoorTV (MOTV) app and Rumble, providing opportunities to showcase Tackle Warehouse’s extensive selection of fishing tackle, equipment and accessories to the tournament fishing community.

“Tackle Warehouse has been a tremendous partner to Major League Fishing and a trusted resource for our anglers, whether they’re gearing up for their first BFL or preparing for a Pro Circuit event,” said Jake Wittkop, MLF Vice President and Managing Director of Sponsorship and Business Development. “Their continued investment in the Pro Circuit and MLF5 helps give anglers the opportunity to compete close to home and work their way up to the national stage. We’re proud to build on this partnership over the next three years.”

The Tackle Warehouse Pro Circuit kicks off Feb. 18-20 at Lake Murray in Columbia, South Carolina, before traveling to Chickamauga Lake in Tennessee, Sam Rayburn Reservoir in Texas, Clarks Hill Lake in Georgia, the Arkansas River in Oklahoma and the St. Lawrence River in New York. The season will culminate Sept. 10-12 at the Pro Circuit Championship on the James River in Richmond, Virginia.

Anglers who aspire to fish the 2027 Tackle Warehouse Pro Circuit may enter by calling Major League Fishing at 270.252.1000.

For more information about MLF, its tournaments and sponsors, visit MajorLeagueFishing.com. To explore Tackle Warehouse’s extensive selection of fishing tackle, equipment and accessories, visit TackleWarehouse.com .

Tackle Warehouse is the premier online shop for all of your bass angling needs. They provide the industry’s best gear, customer service, in-depth knowledge of products, tips and techniques from pros, as well as fast, efficient shipping. For more information visit TackleWarehouse.com   and follow them on social media at Facebook, X,  YouTube  and Instagram.

title: When Everton fans will get first glimpse of new multi-year sponsorship agreement
article_text:
Everton have made an out-of-window signing that is hoped will be a long-term success.

The Toffees have made a number of branding changes in the 2026-27 season already.

CMC Markets took centre stage as the team's new front-of-shirt sponsor, replacing the previous occupier of that position, Stake.

In a resulting move, Stake switched to find their sponsorship place on the sleeves of Everton shirts.

This was done as part of Everton's compliance with the Premier League's new front-of-shirt gambling ban.

Hill Dickinson Stadium chiefs have evidently been continuing to search for fresh commercial agreements, and they've now struck another one.

What benefits will Everton's new sponsor get from partnership deal?

Announced via Everton's club website on Tuesday afternoon, the club have signed a 'multi-year' partnership deal with global technology brand, NOCO.

No concrete details have yet emerged on the figures and fees involved in the agreement.

However, with the company signing on to join Everton for a number of years, it's clearly an important business deal for the club.

Confirming via their website, Everton have revealed that NOCO will receive "prominent brand visibility" around Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Their presence will be seen on advertising boards surrounding the pitch, as well as promotion through Everton's various media channels.

NOCO branding will first appear at an Everton matchday on Sunday, when the latest renewal of the Merseyside derby takes place against Liverpool.

So, who exactly are NOCO, and what official partner are they becoming for Everton?

Why TFG have takeover incentives to cash in on multiple Everton players in January Where are Everton's new sponsors NOCO based?

Founded in Cleveland, Ohio in 1914, NOCO are now headquartered in Glenwillow, Ohio.

They are a privately held American multinational corporation, who largely specialise in the designing, manufacturing and marketing of electronic products.

NOCO are predominantly known for their production of battery chargers and lithium batteries, but produce many other related products.

It's probably no surprise then that they've become Everton's new official battery charging partner.

Of course, this deal represents a fresh wave of American financial investment into Everton alongside The Friedkin Group.

Whether or not this is a targeted and deliberate move by Everton in a wider attempt to increase their standing across the pond, or a coincidence, remains to be seen.

What it should do at a base level is increase the selling value of the football club, as TFG continue to explore a sale.

However, with this deal being announced off the back of Everton's 4-0 thrashing to Brentford, fans may not be overly thrilled by the timing.

title: Baller League launches international women’s competition
article_text:
Baller League has introduced a women’s competition as part of its new Nations Cup, creating an international six-a-side tournament for amateur female players across 16 countries and 64 cities.

The women’s tournament will run alongside a men’s competition, with both winning teams receiving equal $1m prizes. Teams will progress from city-level tournaments to national qualifiers before the 16 national champions compete at the international finals.

The format will allow amateur teams to enter without affiliation to a professional club, academy or agent. Registration is scheduled to open in March 2027, with the competition running from 26th June until the final weekend from 5th-7th November.

The introduction of the women’s tournament represents an expansion of Baller League’s existing six-a-side format. Founded in Germany in 2024, the competition has since established leagues in the UK and United States.

The equal prize allocation means a combined $2m will be awarded to the men’s and women’s champions. Baller League founder and CEO Felix Starck has described each $1m award as what the organisation believes to be the largest prize offered to amateur footballers, although that claim has not been independently verified.

For the UK, the Nations Cup will build on Baller League’s existing domestic presence and provide amateur women’s teams with a route from local competition to representing their country in an international tournament.

title: Arab Cup Qatar 2025 wins Premier Sports Event of the Year Award
article_text:
The FIFA Arab Cup Qatar 2025 won the Qatar Tourism Award for Premier Sports Event of the Year, in recognition of the tournament's outstanding success, strong fan turnout, and contributions to Qatar's economy and tourism sector.

The Local Organizing Committee for Football Events received the award at a ceremony held in Doha, which recognized leading events that have helped strengthen Qatar's position as a premier destination for hosting major sporting events.

The tournament was held from Dec 1 to 18, 2025, with 16 Arab national teams competing across six stadiums that had previously hosted matches during the FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022. A total of 1,220,063 fans attended the 32 matches. The final, held at Lusail Stadium, drew 84,517 spectators, setting a record for the highest attendance in the tournament's history.

The tournament's success extended beyond the sporting arena and fan engagement to include a boost to tourism and economic activity. An economic impact assessment conducted in collaboration with Nielsen Sports, a company specializing in sports analytics, found that the tournament generated a total economic impact of QR2.89 billion for the local economy.

The tournament formed part of an exceptional football season in Qatar in 2025, during which the country hosted the finals of three FIFA competitions within three weeks. These included the inaugural 48-team edition of the FIFA U-17 World Cup Qatar and the FIFA Intercontinental Cup.

Qatar is currently hosting the FIFA U-17 World Cup Qatar 2026 and is preparing to host the final three matches of the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2026, scheduled for Dec 9, 12 and 16.

Qatar continues to strengthen its presence on the global sporting stage by hosting a series of major international competitions, including the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027, the FIFA Arab Cup 2029, the FIVB Volleyball World Championship 2029 and the Asian Games 2030.

title: Ritomo Miyata reflects on his ‘amazing’ first Formula 2 win in Madrid
article_text:
Ritomo Miyata achieved his first Formula 2 victory in the Madrid Sprint Race, and recently we caught up with him to talk through it all.

The Hitech driver converted a P2 start into a win in Saturday’s shorter race, and made it to the podium again on Sunday, going from ninth to third.

Miyata believes his good starting positions were key to his success that weekend, having qualified inside the top 10 for just the third time in the season.

“It was an amazing weekend,” reflected Miyata. “At first this year we struggled, especially with short run performance.

“But in Madrid, we finished inside the top 10 in quali, and then we won the Sprint Race, and we got back to the podium in the Feature Race, finishing P3, and that was really good.

“Actually, we have good long run performance, it’s just we lack a bit in the short run performance. So in Madrid, it was really good.”

Looking more into the Sprint Race win, Miyata spoke about the keys to victory that day.

“With Madrid, the layout looked difficult to overtake on,” he explained. “So, I was trying to focus on my start, because that's the overtake opportunity. But actually my start was good, and then I overtook P1, and then I took the lead of the race.

“Then I managed our pace, but I was expecting it would be chaos because it was so easy to hit the wall, and easy to get a Safety Car. So I tried to do my best with the restarts and then we won.”

It was already a successful weekend for Miyata and Hitech, but a great strategy call to not pit early from the Softs paid off.

The Japanese driver was sat in third when a Safety Car was called and was able to maintain the position once he made his mandatory stop, and held on to take the final spot on the podium.

“In the Feature Race, it was the same as the Sprint, we expected the Safety Car risk,” said Miyata. “Also, in the Sprint Race, a few drivers took the option tyres, so that was good information for the Feature Race.

“We tried to avoid the Safety Car risk. Also, we needed good performance before the pit stop, and actually, before the pit stop, our pace was strong. That's why we could stay on track as long as possible.

“There was a late Safety Car, so we gained some positions. So, that's what helped us finish third in the Feature Race.”

Reflecting on the weekend overall Miyata said: “It was really good because in one weekend, we had two podiums, and that is really difficult. Of course, sometimes it happens, but it's not easy.

“For me, it was my first win in F2, and actually, it was the first podium of my career because last year I gained from some drivers getting penalties at Spa, and I was promoted to P2.

“But this time I actually got to stand on the podium for the first time. So, I didn’t imagine I could get the podium in a Feature Race.

“Also, I was starting in P9. I thought maybe a good result would be P6 or P5. But in the end, we finished P3. It's really good, and a double podium in one weekend. It's really amazing.”

title: Australian Sports Commission and Getty Images Launch Inclusive Community Sport Visual Library
article_text:
The Australian Sports Commission (ASC) has partnered with global visual content creator Getty Images to launch a dedicated visual library designed to modernise how grassroots sport is represented across Australia.

The collection is delivered under Play Well, Australia’s first national sport participation strategy, co-designed with the sector in 2023, and debuts with 250 authentic still images and videos spanning athletics, equestrian, netball, badminton, and football. By resolving a long-standing marketing bottleneck for national sporting organisations (NSOs) and local clubs, the initiative supplies sector-wide communications teams with representative promotional assets ahead of the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

ASC executive general manager of sport system impact and chair of the Play Well Leadership Group, Richard McInnes, highlighted the commercial and participation impact of equipping sports with authentic visual storytelling tools.

“Play Well is built on the belief that everyone has a place in sport.”

“We know the way sport is represented can influence whether people feel welcome and believe there is a place for them.

“This partnership will give sporting organisations access to authentic images, to use in promotional material and communication, that actually reflects the diversity of the people, communities and experiences that make Australian sport so special.

“It is another practical step towards breaking down barriers to participation and ensuring more people can see themselves being involved in sport,” McInnes said.

Getty Images senior director of custom and creative partnerships, Svetlana Zhukova, emphasised the role of representative media in reshaping community perceptions ahead of Brisbane 2032.

“Sport has an extraordinary ability to connect people, but the images used to represent it don’t always reflect who is actually taking part.”

“Through the partnership, we’re giving sports organisations, media and communities access to imagery that better reflects the diversity of Australian sport as the country looks towards Brisbane 2032,” Zhukova said.

Produced in collaboration with community clubs and inclusion bodies—including Sport Inclusion Australia, Metropolitan Districts Netball Association, Footscray Rangers Football Club, and Melbourne Smashers Badminton, the library reflects diverse ages, cultural backgrounds, genders, and physical abilities. Sporting bodies and sector partners can request direct access to the asset bank via the ASC marketing team, with additional sports scheduled for production and integration throughout 2027.
